verses.sanskrit: शरीरं साधनं यस्य जरामरणवर्जितम् | रसायनं तदायाति योगसिद्धिः करस्थिता ||
verses.transliteration: śarīraṃ sādhanaṃ yasya jarāmaraṇa-varjitam | rasāyanaṃ tadāyāti yoga-siddhiḥ karasthitā ||
verses.translation: For one whose body is the instrument, freed from aging and death — the elixir approaches, and yogic accomplishment is in hand.
verses.hindi: जिसका शरीर साधन बन जाए, जो जरा-मरण से रहित हो — उसके लिए रसायन आ जाता है, और योग-सिद्धि करीब है।
verses.commentary: "Śarīraṃ sādhanaṃ" — the body as instrument. This is the central shift the Yoga Rasayanam makes from ascetic traditions that treat the body as an enemy. The body is the sādhana — the means, the tool, the vehicle. But it must be prepared: "jarāmaraṇa-varjitam" — freed from aging and death. This does not mean literal immortality in the Western sense; it means the body is maintained in such vital condition that aging and death do not obstruct the practice. The Hatha Yoga tradition calls this "deha-siddhi" — mastery of the body. The mechanism: rasāyana (rejuvenation) through yogic practice itself — āsana prevents stiffness, prāṇāyāma prevents prāṇa-depletion, mudrā seals the subtle energies, and dhyāna redirects the life-force inward.

verses.translation: One whose body is afflicted with impurities attains purification through the six cleansing acts (ṣaṭkarma). Then, through the practice of āsana, prāṇāyāma, and mudrā, the intellect becomes pure.
verses.hindi: जिसका शरीर मल से आकुलित है, वह षट्कर्म से शुद्धि प्राप्त करता है। तत्पश्चात् आसन, प्राणायाम और मुद्राभ्यास से बुद्धि शुद्ध होती है।
verses.commentary: The sequential logic of Hatha Yoga practice as outlined in the Yoga Rasayanam: (1) Ṣaṭkarma — the six cleansing practices (dhauti, basti, neti, trāṭaka, nauli, kapālabhāti) remove gross impurities (mala) from the digestive, respiratory, and visual systems. Without this preliminary purification, the subtle practices cannot take hold. (2) Āsana — postural practice stabilizes the body and makes it capable of sitting for extended meditation. (3) Prāṇāyāma — breath control regulates the life-force (prāṇa) and begins to shift the nervous system from sympathetic dominance to parasympathetic balance. (4) Mudrā — energetic seals that redirect prāṇa into the central channel (suṣumnā). The sequence matters: you cannot effectively practice prāṇāyāma with a congested digestive system; you cannot hold mudrā with a rigid spine. The Yoga Rasayanam's step-by-step approach is a precise technology, not a random collection of techniques.

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मचर्यं रसायनं योगिनां मोक्षसाधनम् | शुक्र-रक्षणमेवात्र परमं धर्म उच्यते ||
verses.transliteration: brahmacaryaṃ rasāyanaṃ yogināṃ mokṣasādhanam | śukra-rakṣaṇamevātra paramaṃ dharma ucyate ||
verses.translation: Brahmacharya is the elixir, the means of liberation for yogins. The protection of śukra (vital essence/semen) is declared here to be the supreme dharma.
verses.hindi: ब्रह्मचर्य योगियों का रसायन और मोक्ष-साधन है। शुक्र की रक्षा ही यहाँ परम धर्म कही गई है।
verses.commentary: The Yoga Rasayanam's most controversial and most central teaching: brahmacharya as the conservation and sublimation of sexual energy. "Śukra-rakṣaṇa" — protection of śukra. In the Ayurvedic and yogic framework, śukra is not merely reproductive fluid but the distilled essence of all seven dhātus (bodily tissues). The body produces śukra last, after producing rasa (plasma), rakta (blood), māṃsa (muscle), medas (fat), asthi (bone), and majjā (marrow). Śukra is the final, most refined product of the body's alchemical process. To expend it carelessly is to deplete the accumulated essence of the entire organism. To conserve and sublimate it (through yogic practice, not mere suppression) is to accumulate ojas — the vital reserve that sustains long-term practice and prevents aging. The teaching is not anti-sexual but pro-conservation: the energy directed toward reproduction can, through practice, be redirected toward higher consciousness.

verses.sanskrit: सम्यगाहारः सततं सम्यगासनसंस्थितिः | सम्यग्प्राणोऽनिलः शुद्धः सम्यग्ज्ञानं रसायनम् ||
verses.transliteration: samyag āhāraḥ satataṃ samyag āsana-saṃsthitiḥ | samyag prāṇo'nilaḥ śuddhaḥ samyag jñānam rasāyanam ||
verses.translation: Right food always, right posture in sitting, right breath — the pure wind — and right knowledge: this is the rasāyana.
verses.hindi: सदा सम्यक् आहार, सम्यक् आसन-संस्थिति, सम्यक् प्राण (शुद्ध वायु), और सम्यक् ज्ञान — यही रसायन है।
verses.commentary: The four-fold "samyak" (right/correct/complete) rasāyana of the Yoga Rasayanam: (1) Samyag āhāra — right food. Not just healthy eating but eating that supports practice: sāttvika (light, nourishing, non-stimulating), mitahāra (moderate quantity), and eaten with awareness. (2) Samyag āsana-saṃsthiti — right posture. The capacity to sit stable and comfortable for extended periods. Not advanced postures but fundamental sitting capacity. (3) Samyag prāṇa — right breath. The breath is "anilaḥ" (wind) — it must be "śuddhaḥ" (pure/clear). This means not only nasal cleansing but breath that is smooth, even, and without obstruction. (4) Samyag jñānam — right knowledge. The understanding of what the practice actually does and why. Without this, the other three are merely physical techniques. Together, these four constitute the complete rasāyana.

verses.sanskrit: कुण्डलिनी कुलकुण्डली मूलाधारे निवेशिता | उत्थिता सुषुम्नामार्गेण अमृतं स्रावयेत् शिरः ||
verses.transliteration: kuṇḍalinī kulakuṇḍalī mūlādhāre niveśitā | utthitā suṣumnā-mārgeṇa amṛtaṃ srāvayet śiraḥ ||
verses.translation: Kundalini, coiled like a ring, dwells in the mūlādhāra. When she rises through the path of suṣumnā, she causes amṛta to flow from the head.
verses.hindi: कुण्डलिनी, कुण्डली के समान मुड़ी हुई, मूलाधार में स्थित है। जब वह सुषुम्ना-मार्ग से उठती है, तो शिरस (सहस्रार) से अमृत की धारा बहती है।
verses.commentary: The Yoga Rasayanam's most powerful image: the inner medicine. Not herbs, not minerals, not external substances — but the awakening of kuṇḍalinī, the dormant spiritual energy, which when activated produces "amṛta" (nectar of immortality) from the sahasrāra. The physiology: the kuṇḍalinī, represented as a coiled serpent at the base of the spine (mūlādhāra cakra), is awakened through the combined practices of āsana, prāṇāyāma, mudrā, and bandha. She rises through the central channel (suṣumnā nāḍī), piercing each cakra, until she reaches the sahasrāra at the crown. There, she unites with Śiva (pure consciousness), and the resulting union produces amṛta — a subtle biochemical or energetic change that revitalizes the entire organism. The text describes this amṛta flowing back down through the body, producing "jarā-maraṇa-mukti" — freedom from aging and death.

verses.sanskrit: योऽनुभूय परमानन्दममृतरससम्प्लवात् | भस्मीभवन्ति रोगाः स जीवन्मुक्त उदाहृतः ||
verses.transliteration: yo'nubhūya paramānandam amṛta-rasa-samplavāt | bhasmībhavanti rogāḥ sa jīvan-mukta udāhṛtaḥ ||
verses.translation: One who experiences supreme bliss from the flood of amṛta-rasa — for that one diseases are reduced to ash. Such a one is called jīvan-mukta (liberated while living).
verses.hindi: जो अमृत-रस की वृष्टि से परमानंद का अनुभव करता है — उसके रोग भस्म हो जाते हैं। वही जीवन्मुक्त कहलाता है।
verses.commentary: "Amṛta-rasa-samplava" — the flood of nectar-essence. This is the culminating experience of the Yoga Rasayanam path: not merely health, not merely longevity, but the "paramānanda" (supreme bliss) that arises when the inner elixir flows. The effects are described in two stages: (1) "Bhasmībhavanti rogāḥ" — diseases are reduced to ash. The physical body is so vital and the immune system so optimized that disease cannot take hold. (2) "Sa jīvan-muktaḥ" — such a person is liberated while living. Jīvan-mukti is the state in which one is fully awake to the Self while continuing to function in the body. The Yoga Rasayanam's unique contribution: it presents jīvan-mukti not merely as a philosophical attainment but as a physiological possibility — the natural result of maintaining the body as a vessel for awakened consciousness. When the body is rasāyana (full of elixir), the mind is mukta (free).

verses.sanskrit: योगश्चित्तवृत्तिरोधो योगो मोक्षप्रदायकः | योगः सर्वबन्धानां योगो रसायनसमाश्रयः ||
verses.transliteration: yogaścittavṛttirodho yogo mokṣapradāyakaḥ | yogaḥ sarvabandhānāṃ yogaḥ rasāyanasamāśrayaḥ ||
verses.translation: Yoga is the cessation of mental modifications; yoga gives liberation. Yoga cuts all bonds; yoga rests on rasayana.
verses.hindi: योग चित्त-वृत्तियों का निरोध है; योग मोक्ष देता है। योग सभी बंधनों को काटता है; योग रसायन पर आश्रित है।
verses.commentary: The definition of yoga from Yoga Sutras, placed in the context of rasayana practice. Yoga is the cessation of mental modifications, leading to liberation. All bonds are cut through this practice, which rests on the foundation of rasayana (rejuvenation/elixir).
verses.wordMeaning: The definition of yoga from Yoga Sutras, placed in the context of rasayana practice. Yoga is the cessation of mental modifications, leading to liberation. All bonds are cut through this practice, which rests on the foundation of rasayana (rejuvenation/elixir).

verses.sanskrit: अहं ब्रह्मास्मि न त्वं भूतिर्न च भूतानि | सर्वं रसायन एव सर्वं रसायन मयि सर्वम् ||
verses.transliteration: ahaṃ brahmāsmi na tvaṃ bhūtirna ca bhūtāni | sarvaṃ rasāyana eva sarvaṃ rasāyana mayi sarvam ||
verses.translation: I am Brahman, not you; I am birth, not beings; all is rasayana alone, all is rasayana in me.
verses.hindi: मैं ब्रह्म हूँ, तुम नहीं; मैं जन्म हूँ, प्राणी नहीं; सब रसायन ही है, सब रसायन मेरे में है।
verses.commentary: The declaration of non-duality with rasayana as the supreme. The individual Self is Brahman; the world is rasayana (the elixir of life); all distinctions dissolve in this recognition.
verses.wordMeaning: The declaration of non-duality with rasayana as the supreme. The individual Self is Brahman; the world is rasayana (the elixir of life); all distinctions dissolve in this recognition.

verses.sanskrit: यथा नदी समुद्रेषु यथा दीपो दीतेषु | तथा जीवो रसायने लीनो न तत्र संशयो भवति ||
verses.transliteration: yathā nadī samudreṣu yathā dīpo dīpiteṣu | tathā jīvo rasāyane līno na tatra saṃśayo bhavati ||
verses.translation: As rivers merge into the ocean, as lamps merge into light — so the individual self merges into rasayana. There is no doubt about this.
verses.hindi: जैसे नदियाँ समुद्र में लीन हो जाती हैं, जैसे दीप ज्योति में लीन हो जाते हैं — वैसे ही जीव रसायन में लीन हो जाता है। इसमें कोई संशय नहीं।
verses.commentary: The dissolution of individuality into rasayana. The images of rivers into ocean and lamps into light illustrate the loss of separate identity while the essence remains.
verses.wordMeaning: The dissolution of individuality into rasayana. The images of rivers into ocean and lamps into light illustrate the loss of separate identity while the essence remains.

verses.sanskrit: शान्तं शिवमद्वैतं रसायन नित्यं शुद्धमच्युतम् | यो जानाति स पश्यति यो न जानाति न पश्यति ||
verses.transliteration: śāntaṃ śivamadvaitaṃ rasāyana nityaṃ śuddhamacyutam | yo jānāti sa paśyati yo na jānāti na paśyati ||
verses.translation: Peaceful, auspicious, non-dual rasayana — eternal, pure, immutable. He who knows, sees; he who does not know, does not see.
verses.hindi: शांत, शिव, अद्वैत रसायन — नित्य, शुद्ध, अच्युत। जो जानता है, वह देखता है; जो नहीं जानता, वह नहीं देखता।
verses.commentary: The attributes of rasayana: peaceful, auspicious, non-dual, eternal, pure, immutable. Knowledge is seeing; ignorance is blindness.
verses.wordMeaning: The attributes of rasayana: peaceful, auspicious, non-dual, eternal, pure, immutable. Knowledge is seeing; ignorance is blindness.

verses.sanskrit: एको देवो द्वितीयो नास्ति यो रसायनं वेद तत्त्वतः | सोऽहमस्मि न किंचिद्भूतो न मृत्युर्न शोको न तथा ||
verses.transliteration: eko devo dvitīyo nāsti yo rasāyanaṃ veda tattvataḥ | so'hamasmi na kiñcidbhūto na mṛtyurna śoko na tathā ||
verses.translation: There is one God, no second — he who knows rasayana in truth. I am He, not any being, no death, no sorrow, and so on.
verses.hindi: एक ही देव है, दूसरा कोई नहीं — जो रसायन को तत्व से जानता है। मैं वही हूँ, कोई प्राणी नहीं, मृत्यु नहीं, शोक नहीं, वगैरह।
verses.commentary: The affirmation of non-duality: one reality, no second. The knower recognizes "I am He" and transcends death, sorrow, and all suffering.
verses.wordMeaning: The affirmation of non-duality: one reality, no second. The knower recognizes "I am He" and transcends death, sorrow, and all suffering.
